messages:
anya: Heads up — getting flooded with 502/504 reports from hosted-api around 09:46 UTC after the canary that rolled ~09:40. Multiple customers reporting timeouts and gateway errors. Raising here to coord.
kevin: looking. Are we sure it's the canary? any recent config flags or routing changes?
maria: saw the same in the error dashboard — 5xx rate jumped from 0.3% -> 6% in ~5m window. Latency p50 stable but p95 and p99 spiked to 2.3s/8.2s.
dave: @anya can you paste an example request/response from support tickets?
anya: here's a repro from a customer:

curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"Summarize this..."}'

Response:
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"gateway_timeout","message":"upstream read timeout"}

support-bot: attached logs for request id 8a4f2c — upstream returned reset by peer, grpc error code 14.

kevin: grabbing infra logs. PromQL I ran:

sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",code=~"5.."}[1m])) by (route)

kevin: also saw a sharp increase in connection reset errors on the canary pool's NLB.

maria: config audit shows this canary toggled two things: enable_dynamic_batching=true and batch_max_latency_ms=1200. The previous default was batching disabled for v2 route.

anya: that matches timing. A large customer spike could trigger batching to collect many requests and hold them, causing upstream timeouts when the backend fails to keep up. But why resets?
dave: possible kernel socket backlog fill or upstream worker oom leading to connection resets. Let's get pod logs from canary runtime.

incident-bot: deploy event: canary rollout c7f9d4 -> service/routing:v2 flagged at 2025-11-04T09:40:12Z by deploy-bot (user: tina)

tina: cc @kevin I flipped the canary flag to enable_v2_routing for 10% traffic as part of perf test.

kevin: pulling canary runtime logs:

```
[09:41:05] WARN runtime.batch_pool: queue_wait_exceeded count=132
[09:41:06] ERROR runtime.worker: upstream_call failed: grpc: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: read tcp 10.0.0.23:5432->10.0.0.45:54321: read: connection reset by peer"
[09:41:07] ERROR runtime.worker: OOM killed process pid=8721 mem=3.8GB
```

maria: OOMs on canary workers look correlated. dynamic batching increased memory pressure (larger KV cache retention + bigger batch tensors). We probably didn't vet memory footprint for this model+quant setting.

anya: ok-- immediate plan: rollback canary flag to previous state and scale up canary workers/limits while we investigate a safer batching policy.

kevin: agreed. Tina can you roll back the flag to false and trigger canary ablation? @deploy-bot can we patch the flag quickly? :pray:

deploy-bot: running config-toggle --service routing --flag enable_dynamic_batching=false --target canary --author tina

deploy-bot: success — flag toggled. Traffic rebalanced at 09:48:23 UTC.

maria: after rollback 5xx rate dropped back to baseline within two minutes. p99 latency normalizing.

anya: support update: informing affected customers that we reverted the canary and will follow-up with root cause & mitigation.

kevin: follow-up actions:
- add memory/oom guard for canary batches (cap batch_max_tokens and per-batch mem estimator)
- add preflight check on batching flag for models with high KV and quant settings
- automatic rollback threshold: if 5xx rate > 1% within 3m, auto-toggle flag off
- add a chaos-proof runbook for dynamic batching rollouts

dave: capturing repro steps used for debugging:
1) enable_dynamic_batching=true + batch_max_latency_ms=1200
2) send steady stream of 50 req/s with wide sequence length (avg 800 tokens) from 10 clients
3) observe OOMs on canary worker within ~4 minutes

tina: I accidentally left canary size low (2 replicas) and didn't increase pod memory request when enabling batching. That's on me. Will be more careful.

anya: no blame — thanks for quick rollback. For CS: drafting outbound note.

maria: postmortem items and timeline:
- 09:40:12 flag flip -> canary enabled batching
- 09:41:00 perturbation begins, errors start to surface
- 09:44:30 SLO alerts trigger, support escalates
- 09:48:23 rollback completed
- 09:50:00 metrics normalized

kevin: I'll add a temporary alert to catch similar memory OOM patterns even if 5xx not yet spiking.
dave: ops follow-ups: increase canary replica minimum to 4 for future memory-impacting flags, require perf checklist sign-off.

anya: final question — do we want a hotfix to reject batching toggle if model==rwd-13b and quant==q4? or just preflight warnings?
maria: add both: hard reject for now in the flag validation layer, plus advisory message.

tina: will open the PR for flag validation + update runbook. PR will reference this thread.

support-bot: ticket updates queued for 16 customers impacted. Assigned to anya for communications.

anya: thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated with PR links and the postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
